### 주요 대회 상세 정보

**1. 파리 하프마라톤 (3월 7일)**
- **참가비**: €79 (추첨 당첨 시)
- **특징**: 추첨제 운영, 2~6명 팀 신청 가능 (1명 당첨 시 전원 당첨)
- **코스**: 평탄, 남자 코스 기록 59:38 (2023), 여자 1:05:12 (2026)로 기록 잘 나오는 코스
- **접수**: 2026년 9월 8~30일 추첨 신청, 10월 1일 결과 발표 (이미 마감)

**2. 바르셀로나 마라톤 하프 (3월 14일)**
- **참가비**: €94 (하프마라톤)
- **특징**: 세계에서 가장 빠른 코스 중 하나, 2026년 풀코스 여자 우승 기록 2:10:51
- **코스**: 완전 평탄, 도심 코스
- **접수**: 현재 3차 티어 판매 중, 3월 7일 또는 정원 마감 시 종료

**3. 예루살렘 마라톤 (3월 19일)**
- **참가비**: $76 (국제 참가자, 12월 2일 이후 $90, 1월 26일 이후 $95)
- **특징**: 구시가지, 크네세트, 올리브산 등 역사적 명소 통과
- **코스**: 언덕 많음, 하프 고저차 327m, 기록보다는 경관 중심
- **접수**: 3월 13일까지

**4. 바스 하프마라톤 (3월 14일)**
- **참가비**: £55.50 (비소속), £53.50 (클럽 소속)
- **특징**: 영국 전통 대회 (1982년 시작), 에이번 강변 코스
- **코스**: 완만한 언덕, 고저차 90m, 마지막 Royal Avenue 오르막
- **접수**: 현재 접수 중

**5. 리딩 하프마라톤 (3월 21일)**
- **참가비**: £46 (클럽 소속), £48 (비소속)
- **특징**: 영국 대형 하프마라톤, 축구 경기장 피니시
- **코스**: 완만한 언덕, 고저차 140m, Russell Street 오르막 구간
- **접수**: 현재 접수 중

**6. 바쿠 마라톤 (5월 2일)**
- **참가비**: AZN 100 (국제 참가자, 약 $59)
- **특징**: 카스피해 해안 코스, 2026년 첫 풀코스 개최
- **코스**: 평탄, 고저차 80m, 해안 대로 중심
- **접수**: 아직 미개시

**7. 만리장성 마라톤 (5월 15일)**
- **참가비**: 투어 패키지 포함 (6일 $1,790~, 7일 $2,090~)
- **특징**: 세계에서 가장 힘든 마라톤, 5,164개 계단, 만리장성 위 달리기
- **코스**: 극도로 험난, 고저차 1,560m, 기록 도전 불가, 모험 중심
- **접수**: 2월 15일까지 조기 등록 (이후 $150 추가), 투어 패키지 필수

### 참고사항
- 항공권과 숙소 가격은 **목업(실제 가격 아님)**이며, 실제 예약 시 가격이 다를 수 있습니다.
- 접수 마감일과 대회 일정은 공식 사이트에서 재확인하세요.
- 파리 하프마라톤은 추첨제로 이미 추첨 신청이 마감되었습니다.
- 만리장성 마라톤은 개인 접수가 불가하며 투어 패키지로만 참가 가능합니다.

The Lowdown
The Jerusalem Marathon (currently the Winner Jerusalem Marathon under its title sponsor, the Israeli pharmacy chain Winner) is an AIMS-certified international marathon through the historic heart of Jerusalem. Revived in 2011, the race has grown into one of the largest running events in Israel, drawing nearly 40,000 participants across all its distances in recent editions. The 42.2 km marathon course starts at Hamagbit Square near the Knesset and Israel Museum and finishes at the southern end of Sacher Park via the Valley of the Cross, passing landmarks including the President's House, Ammunition Hill, the Mount Scopus campus of the Hebrew University, the Old City's Armenian Quarter and Zion Gate, the Sultan's Pool, and the Emek Refaim neighborhood. The course is notably hilly, with roughly 556 m of total elevation gain on the full marathon (327 m on the half), reflecting Jerusalem's rolling terrain at around 800 m elevation. Held in mid-to-late March, the race benefits from Jerusalem's mild, dry early-spring climate. Title sponsorship of the event has changed hands over the years (it has also been run under the Continental and other sponsor names), so it is listed here under its sponsor-neutral name.

The Zurich Barcelona Marathon 2027 starts at 8:30 on Sunday 14 March from Passeig de Gràcia, and its price has already moved to the third and last tier: the €80 and €90 bibs are sold out and the one on sale is €100, out of 37,000 places managed by RPM Sports with Barcelona City Council. After the 2:04:57 and 2:10:51 run in 2026, the course sits among the four fastest in the world, which is why runners now fly in for it, and that is where the practical questions come from: bib collection happens only on the Friday and Saturday before the race, so the flight has to land by Saturday; name transfers end on 16 February; the cheap entry has no refund; and the six-hour limit means a pace of 8:30 per kilometre. This guide sets out the tiers, the deadlines, the corrals and pacers, and how race morning works in a city whose metro opens at 5:00.
How much is the Barcelona Marathon 2027 and when does registration close?
€100 for a bib in the current tier, after the €80 and €90 tiers sold out, and €94 for Half Marathon entrants; 37,000 places, closing on 7 March. The race starts on 14 March at 8:30 on Passeig de Gràcia with a 6-hour limit; transfers end on 16 February and bibs are collected on 12 and 13 March only.
Bib collection only on Friday and Saturday, so plan the flight around it
Collection closes at 20:00 on Saturday with no race-day exception: anyone flying in must be in Barcelona on the Saturday.
The date that catches travellers is not race day but the day before. Bibs, chips, bags and T-shirts are handed out at the Expo Sports, at a venue the organisers have yet to announce, on Friday 12 March from 15:00 to 20:00 and Saturday 13 March from 9:00 to 20:00, and the rules are explicit that Saturday at 20:00 is the deadline: there is no collection on the Sunday and no exception. You need a passport or ID card and the e-mail with your bib number, entry to the Expo is free, and medal engraving can be bought there if you skipped it online. A flight landing on Saturday evening therefore does not work; Saturday lunchtime does, with the 
airport to city centre
 options taking 25 to 40 minutes. On race morning the 
metro
 opens at 5:00 every day, and Passeig de Gràcia has stations on lines 2, 3 and 4 within a few hundred metres of the start, so nobody needs a taxi through a closed city centre; a single ticket is €2.90 and the T-casual multi-ride card, €13 for ten journeys, covers the whole weekend. Tap water is safe to drink, which matters more the day before a marathon than any restaurant, and dinner in Barcelona is served late, from about 20:30, so Saturday’s pasta is an early sitting.

What the bib costs by tier, and which package is worth it
The two cheap tiers are gone: register now and you pay €100, or €94 if you also run the Half. The packages are services, not better bibs.
The rules set the price by bib number rather than by date, so the increases arrive without warning: when a tier sells out, the next costs €10 more. The €100 tier is the last and the longest, bibs 16,001 to 37,000, which means entering in autumn or in the week before closing costs the same, as long as places remain. The one real discount goes to entrants in the Hyundai Barcelona Half Marathon 2027, who pay €94 verified against their ID number, at the price of not being able to transfer the bib; for anyone already planning both races that is €6 back, for anyone else the Half costs more than it saves. The Race Experience at €167.85 and Full Experience at €218.90 do not buy a better start; they buy a photo pack, an engraved medal, a keyring and a print, and the one thing that matters to a traveller, refund cover, which the basic Race Entry does not include. Booking fees are added at checkout. Against Berlin, Chicago or London prices the bib is cheap; what it costs to be in Barcelona for the weekend is in the 
daily budget guide
.

Pace, corrals and pacers, and what the six-hour limit means
The 6-hour limit allows 8:30 min/km; pacers stop at 4:30, and slower than that you run alone.
The limit is six hours counted from the last runner’s start, with the course closing around 16:15, which works out at 8:30 per kilometre or 13:41 per mile: fast walking with stretches of running gets you home, strolling does not. Thirty-five pacers run seven finish times from 2:45 to 4:30 in quarter-hour steps, and there is nobody slower than 4:30, so back-of-the-pack runners pace themselves. You pick a corral at registration by predicted time and it cannot be changed afterwards, which is worth being honest about, since the staggered waves exist to stop crowding. The sub-elite corral is granted by e-mail on proof of a result from the last two years in an official race: under 1:05 in the half or 2:20 in the marathon for men, 1:15 or 2:35 for women. Runners must be 18 on race day; no minors, pushchairs, bikes, skates or any assisted device. The course itself is fully urban and flat, which is how Chelangat ran 2:04:57 and Tesfay 2:10:51 in 2026, the latter on her marathon debut; the detailed map, GPX file and start and finish plans are published by the organisers, and the race also hosted the Spanish championship that year. seafront running routes
 and 
where to run in Barcelona
 cover flat kilometres by the water.
Making a weekend of it
The marathon falls in mid-March, before the tourist season and its hotel prices, and the race weekend fits a three-night stay: arrive Friday or Saturday morning, collect the bib, eat early on Saturday, run Sunday, and keep Monday for the city. Where to sleep is the decision the race does not make for you; the 
neighbourhoods to stay in
 explains why the Eixample puts you within walking distance of the start and the finish. The month also brings the run-up to Sant Jordi and the first spring festivals in the 
festivals calendar
, and a 
free afternoon
 on the Monday costs nothing after a €100 bib.

The Lowdown
The Bath Half Marathon is one of the United Kingdom's longest-running road races, held in the historic Georgian city of Bath since 1982 and now the largest one-day charity fundraising event in South West England, having raised more than £30 million for charity since 2000. The race exits Royal Victoria Park and follows a flat, largely traffic-free course along the north bank of the River Avon before finishing with a climb up Royal Avenue, just past the famous Royal Crescent. More than 12,500 runners took part in the 2026 edition. London Marathon Events, organizer of the TCS London Marathon, acquired the race in 2024, and from 2025 it has run as the GetPRO Bath Half under a three-year title partnership, following earlier sponsors including Simplyhealth and EDF Energy. The 2027 edition takes place on Sunday, March 14, with the finish line closing at 16:00, giving entrants at least four and a half hours to complete the course. Entrants must be at least 17 years old on race day. A free companion event, the GetPRO Bath Miles (1 mile), runs the day before. Charity places are available through numerous partner organizations, typically requiring a modest entry fee plus a fundraising pledge of around £250.

The Lowdown
The Reading Half Marathon is an annual road race held every March in Reading, Berkshire, in southern England. First run in 1983 when it started at Reading University with 5,000 runners, it has grown into one of the UK's largest half marathons, with organizers reporting more than 15,000 spectators lining the route on race day. The single-lap, closed-road course starts at Green Park Business Park, loops past the University of Reading's Whiteknights campus and the ruins of Reading Abbey, runs through the town centre, climbs Russell Street in West Reading, and finishes at Select Car Leasing Stadium, home of Reading Football Club. The event has carried several sponsor names over the decades, including Digital, Asics, Mizuno, Vitality, and Sage; Green Park became headline partner from the 2025 edition, and the race is now also marketed as the Green Park Reading Half Marathon. A companion Mini Marathon for younger runners takes place the same morning. Reading Half Marathon is one of the UK's biggest half marathon charity fundraisers, having raised more than half a million pounds for good causes in 2025, and was one of the first town road races to include a wheelchair category. Entries for the 2027 edition on Sunday, March 21, 2027 are open now, with separate pricing tiers for UK Athletics-affiliated and unaffiliated runners.

Kyoto has a humid subtropical climate, which means hot, humid summers and cool winters. Runners should prepare for the heat of summer, where average high temperatures are near 33C (92F), and nights stay very warm. Walking is, of course, a classic way to explore the city. When browsing books on Kyoto, you often see headings like “Kyoto Walking Routes” or “Strolling Through Kyoto.” However, Kyoto is also a wonderful place to run. Here are three main reasons why:
Reason 1: Few Steep Hills
Kyoto sits in a basin surrounded by mountains on three sides, which means the central city is relatively flat. With the exception of some hilly areas in the east and north, there are very few steep slopes, making it easy and comfortable to run.
Reason 2: History, City Life, and Nature—All in One
From World Heritage temples and shrines to the natural setting of the Kamo River, and from business districts to residential neighborhoods, Kyoto brings many layers together in a compact area. Running through the city allows you to experience its history, culture, and living traditions all at once. Feeling the city’s terrain directly is part of the appeal.
Reason 3: Easy Navigation, Fewer Wrong Turns
Central Kyoto is laid out in a grid pattern—often described as a “checkerboard.” This dates back to the construction of the Heian period capital (794) using a Chinese-style grid-based planning system at the time. As long as you keep a rough sense of direction, it’s easy to avoid getting lost. Also, with relatively few high-rise buildings, landmarks are easy to spot: Mt. Daimonji to the east, Kyoto Tower to the south—helpful visual cues that make orientation simple, especially for visitors.
Kyoto is great for walking—but it’s just as enjoyable for running.
Finish an early-morning run and enjoy breakfast, or combine a run with sightseeing. The city is also home to many old-fashioned public bathhouses, perfect for easing tired muscles afterward. A sauna session is another great way to refresh and unwind.
Here, we’ve selected five short running courses (2–6 km) that are easy to enjoy even during short breaks in your travel schedule. Each course starts near a conveniently located station.

Kinukake-no-Michi Route: Run Through Three World Heritage Sites
Approx. 2.5 km / about 15 minutes
Gentle uphill
Our first recommendation starts at Omuro Ninna-ji Station on the Randen Line, heading north-northwest from Kyoto Station. The route passes three Buddhist temples that are World Heritage sites—Ninna-ji Temple, Ryōan-ji Temple, and ends near Kinkaku-ji Temple—along the scenic Kinukake-no-Michi road.
From Omuro Ninna-ji Station, enter Kinukake-no-Michi and follow the road. After a large S-curve heading northeast, you’ll see the entrance to Ryōan-ji Temple on your left. Soon, Ritsumeikan University appears on the right and the Kyoto Prefectural Insho Domoto Museum of Fine Arts on the left—signaling that Kinkaku-ji Temple is close.
The route is simple, but a gentle uphill continues throughout, so a relaxed pace is recommended. Sidewalks are narrow, and during peak tourist seasons there may be more people walking or waiting for buses, but please run with care and avoid getting off the sidewalks.
The name of the road Kinukake-no-Michi  (literally, the “cloth shrouded” road) comes from Mt. Kinugasa, a modest 201-meter hill located roughly between Ryōan-ji Temple and the Domoto Museum—see if you can spot it.
(Route summary)

Approx. 2.5 km (about 15 minutes at 6 min/km)
Kyoto Station Route: From Modern Architecture to Some of Japan’s Largest Temples
Subtle bends in Karasuma Street
Approx. 2.7 km / about 17 minutes
This course begins at Kyoto Station, the city’s main gateway. From the station building, run past two of the largest Buddhist temples—Higashi Hongan-ji Temple and Nishi Hongan-ji Temple—then loop back to Kyoto Station.
Although the area around Kyoto Station is filled with office buildings and large commercial facilities, you’ll soon encounter the impressive Goeido Gate of Higashi Hongan-ji Temple. The forecourt has been redeveloped into a spacious plaza with wider sidewalks and clean public restrooms. Continue west along Shinhanaya-cho Street to Horikawa Street, where Nishi Hongan-ji Temple—another World Heritage site—comes into view.
One point of interest on this route is the set of “bending streets.” While Kyoto’s roads are generally straight, both Karasuma Street near Higashi Hongan-ji Temple and Horikawa Street near Nishi Hongan-ji Temple curve slightly eastward. This dates back to Meiji-period (1868-1912) road widening projects, when streets were rerouted to avoid temple precincts for tram lines. The shift is subtle on maps but noticeable on site.

Kyoto Station → Higashi Hongan-ji Temple→ Nishi Hongan-ji Temple→ Kyoto Station

The tranquil Myojin-gawa stream running through the historic shrine district
Approx. 4.5 km / about 27 minutes
Escape the city bustle in the Kitayama area. Start from Kitayama Station (Exit 1), about 15 minutes by subway from Kyoto Station. The route passes the traditional neighborhood near Kamigamo-jinja Shrine where the Shinto shrine priests have lived, follows the Kamo River, and finishes at Kitaōji Station.
The first half winds through quiet residential streets, so watch for cars on narrower roads. After passing Ota Shrine, famous for its irises, the road opens up and reveals the atmospheric shrine-priest neighborhood (Shake-machi) of Kamigamo-jinja Shrine’s clergy.
The Shake-machi area preserves the old landscape well, including the carefully maintained riverside scenery of Myojin-gawa with small bridges, gates, and benches make this an ideal rest spot. Continue past Kamigamo-jinja Shrine and run south along the Kamo River, then onto Nakaragi-no-Michi, known for its weeping cherry trees.
Note that the adjacent Kyoto Botanical Gardens, which recently marked its 100th anniversary, is part of the Kyoto Marathon course but is not open for regular jogging.

The 2027 Berlin Marathon Lottery Is Now Open
Runners have until Nov. 12 to enter the draw for the Sept. 26, 2027 race, and those who get a place on Dec. 3 will pay €215 ($244).
Published: 
Oct 1, 2026 10:45 am
Jessy Carveth
Jessy Carveth
Jessy is our Senior News Editor, pro cyclist and former track and field athlete with a Bachelors degree in Kinesiology.

Runners hoping to start the 2027 
Berlin Marathon
 can now put their names into the draw. The lottery opened on Thursday, Oct. 1, and stays open until Nov. 12, and everyone who enters will find out by email on 
Dec. 3
 whether they have a place. The race is on Sunday, Sept. 26, 2027, and it will be the first one held under a new name, with the insurer Generali 
taking over as title sponsor
 from BMW, whose name had been on the race since 2011.
Entering the lottery is free, and the fee is charged only to runners whose names come out. For 2027 it is 
€215 ($244)
, which is €10 ($11) more than runners paid for this year’s race, according to the 
official registration page
. Payment is taken from Dec. 4 and can take up to a week to go through, depending on the bank. That money buys a four-day public transport pass for Berlin’s A, B and C fare zones, pacers in every start wave, massage on the course and at the finish, and a poncho once you cross the line, or a bag drop for an extra €5 ($6) if you would rather have your own clothes.

Three Ways Into the Draw
Every applicant picks one of three routes when they register, and that choice is final. Most will enter as individuals. Groups of two or three can apply as a team instead: the first runner registers and receives a team code, the others use it during their own registration, and if the team is drawn, everyone on it gets a place. The code has to go in during registration, so friends planning to run together should sort it out before anyone applies.
The third route is for fast runners, who upload proof of a marathon run in 2025 or 2026 at a race that is AIMS-certified, listed by USATF, or part of the World Marathon Majors age group rankings. Organizers check each proof and tell runners whether they have been accepted when the lottery results go out, so even a qualifying time is no guarantee. Anyone whose proof fails the check is moved into the general draw. The standards themselves are the same times that applied for 2026.
